questions.question: What does eye contact with other drivers mean?

options.text: It is the best way to know they see you.
It is not worth your effort.
It does not guarantee they will yield to you.
It guarantees they will yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not guarantee they will yield to you.
questions.explanation: Never assume eye contact means a driver will yield to you. Many drivers look directly at motorcyclists but do not see them.

questions.question: What should you NOT check on your tires?
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tire air pressure, tread, and general wear. You do not need to check flexibility.

questions.question: What is the correct rule for passing another vehicle?

options.text: Complete the pass without exceeding the speed limit.
You can finish the pass in a no passing zone if you started before it.
You can exceed the speed limit to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Complete the pass without exceeding the speed limit.
questions.explanation: All passes must follow posted speed limits and happen only where passing is allowed.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Speed up to get distance between you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The safest way is to move them in front of you. Change lanes and let them pass if you can do so safely. Speeding up only makes them tailgate at higher speeds, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: What is another name for downshifting to a lower gear?
questions.explanation: Shifting to a lower gear slows you down like using brakes. This is called engine braking.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: When should you use a larger cushion of space between your motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: When it is colder than normal.
When you are following other motorcycles.

questions.explanation: Use a two-second following distance normally. Use more space when roads are icy or wet because you will need more distance to stop.

questions.question: What should you do if a tire goes flat while riding?

options.text: Use both brakes and stop fast.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the road edge.
Relax your grip on the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the road edge.
questions.explanation: Hold the handlebars firmly, ease off the throttle, and stay straight. Brake slowly on the tire that is not flat. As you slow down, move to the road edge, squeeze the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: What material are motorcycle riding gloves usually made from?
questions.explanation: Motorcycle riding gloves are usually made of leather. They improve your grip and protect your hands and fingers.

questions.question: Which action does NOT help a rider increase visibility?

options.text: Using your headlight at all times

questions.explanation: To be visible, wear bright clothes with reflective materials, use your headlight at all times, and use your signals and brake light correctly. Waving does not help visibility.

questions.question: When securing a load, where should you place it?

options.text: Only on one side of the motorcycle.

questions.explanation: Keep loads low and centered. Placing them high raises the motorcycle's center of gravity and makes it harder to balance. Distribute weight evenly on both sides to keep the bike stable.

questions.question: If your front wheel locks up, what should you do?

options.text: Continue to hold the brake and the skid should end.
Release the front brake and do not use it again.
Release the front brake and then quickly squeeze it again.
Release the front brake right away and apply it smoothly again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away and apply it smoothly again.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks, release the front brake completely right away. Then apply the brake smoothly.

questions.question: When making a normal stop, what should you do?

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.
Use only the rear brake to save the front brake.
Use only the front brake to save the rear brake.
Squeeze only the front brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop. This habit helps you stop quickly and safely when needed.

questions.question: Which item is NOT protective riding gear?
questions.explanation: Good protective gear includes a leather jacket, ankle-covering boots, and hearing protection. Wear pants made of leather or sturdy material, not soft material.

questions.question: If your front tire goes flat while riding, what happens?
questions.explanation: A flat front tire makes steering feel heavy. If you notice heavy steering, leave the road and check your tires right away.

questions.question: What is true about approved helmets?

options.text: They can limit how far you can see.
They let you see as far to the sides as you need to.
You do not have to wear one if it limits your view.

questions.correctAnswerText: They let you see as far to the sides as you need to.
questions.explanation: Approved helmets do not dangerously limit your vision. They allow you to see as far to the sides as you need for safe riding.

questions.question: When riding downhill on a motorcycle with a sidecar, how is stopping different?

options.text: Stopping is easier than without a sidecar.
Stopping takes longer than without a sidecar.
Stopping is about the same as without a sidecar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stopping takes longer than without a sidecar.
questions.explanation: A sidecar adds weight, which means you need more braking power to stop. Stopping takes longer going downhill and with extra weight.

questions.question: If another driver is tailgating you, what should you do?

options.text: Change lanes safely and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes safely and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. Change lanes and let them pass if it is safe to do so. Speeding up will only make them tailgate you at a higher speed.

questions.question: When riding, which part of the lane should you use?
questions.explanation: There is no one lane position to always avoid. Change your position based on road conditions to stay safe.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection, what assumption should you make?

options.text: Assume other drivers see you, especially if they make eye contact.
Never assume other drivers see you.
Stay focused on moving through the intersection.
Speed up so others notice you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never assume other drivers see you.
questions.explanation: Never assume other drivers see you, even if they look at you. Drivers often look directly at motorcycles and still do not notice them. Always slow down when approaching an intersection.

questions.question: When braking, what should you do?

options.text: Squeeze the front brake and press the rear brake.
Grab the front brake and squeeze the rear brake.
Press hard on the front brake and grab the rear brake.
Press the front brake and press hard on the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Squeeze the front brake and press the rear brake.
questions.explanation: To brake safely, squeeze the front brake lever and press down on the rear brake pedal. Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: What is a good way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Move onto the shoulder to let them pass.
Speed up to create distance between you.
Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. If it is safe, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up can make the situation more dangerous.

questions.question: Which sign is rectangular?
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white background and black letters or symbols. These signs tell you the rules of the road. You must follow all rules on these signs.

questions.question: When should you use both brakes to slow or stop?

options.text: Only when the pavement is wet.

questions.explanation: Using both the front and rear brakes together gives you the most stopping power. You should use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Where should a child passenger sit?

options.text: They do not need to reach the footrests.
They should hold onto the motorcycle frame.

questions.explanation: A child passenger should always sit directly behind the operator. A child in front may lose balance and could block the operator's controls.
